channel.title: Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty (rferl.org)

item.title: Israeli NGO Head Ksenia Svetlova: Iran Still 'Firing Like Crazy'
item.description: Israel has made an impressive start to military operations against Iran, but may be not much closer to its goals than a week ago, former Knesset member Ksenia Svetlova told RFE/RL in an interview at her home in Tel Aviv.

item.title: After A Week Of War, Israel Sees Progress But Long Road Ahead
item.description: After a dramatic week of air strikes on Iran, what’s the view from Tel Aviv on the progress of the war and what happens next?

item.title: Trump Says Does Not Want Iranian Kurds To Launch Offensive
item.description: Iran's leadership has been hit hard with Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and other senior officials killed in US and Israeli air strikes that continue to pound Tehran and other parts of the country. RFE/RL has continuing updates and analysis.

item.title: Iran War Ripples Across Middle East, Caucasus With New Attacks
item.description: The war in Iran is widening across the Middle East and beyond, with incidents stretching from the Persian Gulf to the South Caucasus and raising fears the conflict could escalate into a broader regional confrontation.

item.title: With Top Brass Dead, Iran Deploys Decentralized 'Mosaic' Strategy To Boost Defenses
item.description: Iran has activated a decentralized defense strategy after the United States and Israel launched an air campaign against Tehran and killed senior military leaders.

item.title: 'We Have Lost Everything': Iranians Continue To Cross Into Armenia Amid Air Attacks
item.description: Iranians cross the border into Armenia as air strikes pound Tehran and other parts of the country. After entering Armenia, one woman said Iranians had "lost everything" amid the destruction and dwindling resources.

item.title: A Russian Soldier Thought He'd Be Deployed To Africa. When They Ordered Him To Ukraine, He Fled.
item.description: When Georgy Kochkin signed up with a Russian military unit called Africa Corps, he was expecting to be deployed to Africa, helping run information security operations. Instead, he was ordered to deploy to Ukraine. So he went AWOL and jumped a plane to Manila, where he told RFE/RL about his story.

item.title: US 'Looking At' Potential Candidates To Lead Iran, As Tehran's Assembly Of Experts Expected To Convene
item.description: Iran's Assembly of Experts is set to meet to select a new supreme leader, one of its members said on March 7, as the White House vowed to look for an "acceptable" candidate to lead the country.

item.title: Cracks In Iranian Leadership? Apology, Then More Regional Attacks
item.description: Iran could be moving closer to electing a new supreme leader even as some cracks appeared to be developing among the surviving leaders in Tehran, while the United States and Israel vowed to hit Iran harder than ever before as the war passes the one-week mark.

item.title: Russian Strike On Kharkiv Residential Building Kills At Least 10, Ukraine Says
item.description: At lease 10 people were killed early on March 8 after Russia struck the northeast Ukrainian city of Kharkiv with missiles and drones, local officials said, prompting an angry call by President Volodymyr Zelenskyy for action by Western partners.
